waypoints.name: Barnette graph G
waypoints.what: Cubic, bipartite, 3-connected, planar. The claim is that G has a Hamiltonian cycle, and more: one that avoids any prescribed edge.

waypoints.name: Dual Eulerian triangulation (T, t0, e0)
waypoints.what: T = G* is a simple sphere triangulation with faces coloured black and white. Root it at a black face t0 with an edge e0. Vertices of G are faces of T, faces of G are vertices of T.

waypoints.name: Two induced trees
waypoints.what: The goal in dual form. G has a Hamiltonian cycle avoiding e0* if and only if V(T) splits into two sets, each inducing a tree, with both ends of e0 in one of them (Stein 1971; APSW 2016).

waypoints.name: States
waypoints.what: A state is a bijection s from the bounded black faces A to the non-root vertices X with s(t) a corner of t. It is a perfect matching of the incidence graph B. |A| = |X| = n.

waypoints.name: A pair (r, s)
waypoints.what: Two states that differ at every face. The partner r is the certificate that orients Q_s: the edge opposite s(t) in t is directed out of r(t).

waypoints.name: Disk identity
waypoints.what: A directed cycle of state edges of length h with l black faces of its disk along it has 2l - h = -3. Equivalently its disk holds exactly one more white face than black faces.

waypoints.name: Signed measure on pairs
waypoints.what: Every pair gets a sign (i^J in O, (-1)^cw in L, epsilon in T). Reversing a cycle of D(r, s) flips it, and reversing a cycle of Q_s flips it. The whole proof is one signed sum over pairs, weighted by a function of s.

waypoints.name: Cancellation of cyclic Q_s
waypoints.what: Sum with s fixed. If Q_s has a cycle, reversing it changes r, keeps s and the weight, and flips the sign. So only pairs with Q_s a forest survive.

waypoints.name: Nonvanishing
waypoints.what: Sum with the undirected cycle set D fixed. With weights whose circulation is positive on every counterclockwise spoke cycle, the lowest-order term is a positive count of the covers with fewest cycles.

waypoints.name: Forest pair / tree matching
waypoints.what: A pair with Q_s a forest. Equivalently a state s with H - s a spanning tree of the spoke graph. Equivalently a state with exactly one partner.

waypoints.name: Incidence tree H - s
waypoints.what: Delete the n matched spokes from the spoke graph H. What is left is a spanning tree: every black centre keeps two spokes, t0 keeps three.

waypoints.name: White-face tree
waypoints.what: The duals of the n deleted spokes form a spanning tree on the white faces (tree-cotree duality in the plane).

waypoints.name: Selected edges P
waypoints.what: Root the white tree at y0, the white face across e0. Each tree edge selects one side of its black face. With e0 this is one edge in every face of T, a perfect matching of G.

waypoints.name: Jordan curve
waypoints.what: E(G) - P is 2-regular. It is a single cycle, hence a Jordan curve on the sphere, and its two sides are the two induced trees.

waypoints.name: Gluing
waypoints.what: If a separating triangle blocks the state method at this root, cut along it, cap both sides, solve each with the cap edge prescribed, and glue.

waypoints.name: Hamiltonian cycle
waypoints.what: Every Barnette graph has a Hamiltonian cycle avoiding any prescribed edge (O Theorem 1.1, Corollary 7.1).

steps.title: Dualise and root
steps.must: 3-connected cubic plane graphs are the duals of simple triangulations, and bipartite means the faces of T 2-colour. This is the only place 3-connectivity is used.
steps.freedom: No freedom in the statement. Li keeps the primal language through the auxiliary graph aux(G); the objects are the same.

steps.title: Restate the goal
steps.must: A Hamiltonian cycle of G is a Jordan curve; the faces of G on each side are vertices of T inducing a tree. Known since Stein. All pre-2026 attacks tried to cross here directly.
steps.freedom: This is the edge that 57 years of partial results worked on. None of them reaches all Barnette graphs.

steps.title: Define states and count
steps.must: Euler's formula gives equally many black and white faces k and k + 2 vertices, so |A| = |X| = k - 1. Without this equality there is nothing to match.
steps.freedom: States are Tutte's trinity states with the colours swapped. Their number is a determinant.

steps.title: Find two disjoint states
steps.must: The incidence graph B must contain two edge-disjoint perfect matchings. This is where a separating triangle can obstruct, and the only place the papers use 'no separating triangle'.
steps.freedom: Four published arguments (flow with a density bound; Ore deficiency with a minimal set; the exact criterion; Hall on a gadget in the Lean proof). They prove different amounts.

steps.title: Prove the disk identity
steps.must: Euler's formula on the disk, a signed count of sides, and B = I + l, which holds because a state is a bijection.
steps.freedom: One double count in all three papers, on triangles (O, T) or on hexagons of the spoke graph (L). A second derivation, as the theorem of turning tangents for an angle structure, is proved in the topology folder and unreviewed.

steps.title: Sign the pairs
steps.must: Define the sign and show that both reversals flip it. The disk identity is used twice here: on the cycles of D and on the cycle of Q_s.
steps.freedom: Three notations for one sign. The complex phase is packaging; a real sign is enough.

steps.title: Cancel with s fixed
steps.must: The reversed cycle of Q_s must be chosen from s alone, so that the map is an involution that keeps the weight.
steps.freedom: All three papers use the same involution. It is the statement that a twisted incidence determinant of Q_s vanishes on a cycle.

steps.title: Show the total is not zero
steps.must: Weights that depend on s only and separate the two orientations of every D-cycle. Then group by D and find a term that cannot cancel.
steps.freedom: The widest step: five published arguments, two more proved here, and a long list of refuted shortcuts. Every route that works still minimises over the number of cycles.

steps.title: Compare the two evaluations
steps.must: The same sum is supported on forest pairs (by K) and is not zero (by N). So a forest pair exists.
steps.freedom: The comparison is one line. No canonical forest pair is known: every extremal choice tried is refuted.

steps.title: Unsigned routes (bypass)
steps.must: Find a tree matching with no signed sum: as a prescribed-degree spanning tree, a three-matroid intersection, a constrained white tree, a point of the state lattice.
steps.freedom: Many exact reformulations are proved. None has an existence argument. Every relaxation tried drops a constraint and is refuted by a small example.

steps.title: One root per component
steps.must: The partner gives out-degree one at non-roots and zero at roots, so a tree component of Q_s has exactly one root. With the three spokes of t0 this makes H - s a spanning tree.
steps.freedom: Same count in all three papers. A forest without a partner is not enough.

steps.title: Tree-cotree duality
steps.must: The complement of a spanning tree of a plane graph is a spanning tree of the dual.
steps.freedom: Rigid as a statement. The Lean proof skips the node: it selects P inside G and never builds the white tree.

steps.title: Root at y0 and select
steps.must: Orient the white tree towards y0; the edge above each white face selects one side of a black face.
steps.freedom: Rigid. The three papers select the same set P.

steps.title: Show P leaves one cycle
steps.must: P has one edge in every face of T, so E(G) - P is 2-regular. It must be connected.
steps.freedom: Two published arguments. O, T and the Lean proof count against the disk identity (a third use). Li uses an innermost cycle and needs neither the disk identity nor the partner.

steps.title: Sides of the curve
steps.must: The two sides of the Jordan curve are the two induced trees, and e0 lies in one of them.
steps.freedom: Li skips this node and glues Hamiltonian cycles directly.

steps.title: Cut at separating triangles
steps.must: The prescribed edge is what lets two solutions agree on the cap. An unbounded prescription would be NP-hard.
steps.freedom: Same induction in all three papers, known since Kelmans 1986. The trees paper cuts less often.

steps.title: Conclude
steps.must: Induction on the number of vertices, or a minimum counterexample.

routes.label: duality; 3-connectivity gives a simple T
routes.where: O proof of Thm 1.1; APSW 2016 Section 1
routes.text: The dual of a 3-connected cubic plane graph is a simple triangulation; G bipartite iff T Eulerian iff the faces of T 2-colour iff the vertices 3-colour.

routes.label: stay in G with aux(G)
routes.text: Li works in the primal graph with the face/black-vertex incidence graph. aux(G) is T with a centre in every face.

routes.label: 3-connectivity enters only here
routes.text: In O, 3-connectivity is used once, to exclude loops and parallel edges in the dual. Simplicity is then used in the flow bound and the gluing.

routes.label: drop bipartite
routes.text: Without bipartiteness there is no proper face colouring of T, so states are not defined.
routes.lesson: Odd degrees obstruct the algebra itself, before any question of Hamiltonicity. Best max-cut colourings of K4, BBL38 and Tutte's graph leave 2, 7 and 9 monochromatic adjacencies.
routes.cex: K4 (4 vertices): the dual has all degrees odd. Tutte's 46-vertex graph is the non-Hamiltonian witness.

routes.label: drop 3-connectivity
routes.text: A 2-connected cubic bipartite planar graph can be non-Hamiltonian. Its dual has parallel edges.
routes.lesson: The proof stops at the pair: the 26-vertex theta of three cubes-minus-an-edge has 8 states and no disjoint pair at each of its 26 roots. The disk identity itself survives in the multimap.
routes.cex: theta of three copies of cube-minus-edge, 26 vertices (minimum by Asano-Saito-Exoo-Harary 1982, abstract only).

routes.label: other surfaces
routes.text: On an orientable surface of genus g, |A| - |X| = 2g, so states with three roots do not exist for g > 0, and the two-tree target is impossible on the torus by an edge count.
routes.lesson: The first obstruction is cardinality. A surface version needs a different state and a different target (one edge per triangle with connected complementary dual).
routes.cex: 3 x 3 periodic triangular grid on the torus: no two induced trees, yet the dual has 36 Hamiltonian cycles.

routes.label: Stein 1971; APSW Lemma 5
routes.where: Stein, Pacific J. Math. 37 (1971), Thm 2.2; APSW 2016, Lemma 5
routes.text: T* is Hamiltonian iff V(T) splits into two induced forests, which for triangulations are two induced trees.

routes.label: prescribed edge: O Theorem 2.2
routes.text: With e0 inside one tree the cycle avoids e0*. This is the H- form of Kelmans and Hertel, equivalent to the conjecture.

routes.label: face-size results (Goodey; Schnieders)
routes.text: Hamiltonicity when all faces have size at most 6 (Goodey), at most 8 (Schnieders, 339 million computer cases). Partial: local reductions cannot see 3-connectivity, which becomes necessary at face size 10.

routes.label: computer search to 90 vertices
routes.text: All Barnette graphs up to 90 vertices are Hamiltonian.

routes.label: trees of faces (Feder-Subi)
routes.text: Contract a colour class of faces and look for a quasi spanning tree of faces. Polynomial when the remaining faces have 2 or 3 sides, NP-complete in general. The closest older relative of the incidence tree.

routes.label: A-trails, braces, book embeddings
routes.text: Equivalent formulations in other languages. None supplied an existence mechanism.

routes.label: trees from colour classes
routes.text: Build a permeating subtree containing all or none of a colour class of the vertex 3-colouring.
routes.lesson: APSW give Eulerian triangulations in which every permeating subtree contains at least k and misses at least k vertices of every colour class. The trees of the 2026 proofs come from a matching, not from colour classes.
routes.cex: APSW 2016, family for every k (not reconstructed here).

routes.label: Grinberg obstruction
routes.where: hist/WHAT-WAS-HARD.md 2; gt/PROOFS.md (Grinberg's identity is automatic for two induced trees)
routes.text: Use Grinberg's formula with a modulus to decide Hamiltonicity.
routes.lesson: A Barnette graph has f_4 = 6 + sum (k/2 - 3) f_k, so at least six faces of weight 2 and the classical modulus argument cannot apply. PROVED-HERE in the history folder.
routes.cex: Any Barnette graph: at least six 4-faces.

routes.label: induced-forest completion
routes.text: Start from a large induced forest and exchange vertices until both sides are trees.
routes.vivid: Farthest from the pair machinery. The general Albertson-Berman conjecture cannot be an input: 2026 preprints report counterexamples.
routes.test: Enumerate maximum induced forests on small Eulerian triangulations and look for a trapped configuration.

routes.label: nodal domains of eigenvectors
routes.text: Sign patterns of Laplacian eigenvectors of T almost never give two induced trees (predicted below 5 per cent).
routes.test: Run over the sample of the topology agent; outcome pending in topo/ROUTES.md.

routes.label: Euler count |A| = |X|
routes.text: k black faces, k white faces, k + 2 vertices, so n = k - 1 on both sides of B.

routes.label: states = trinity states; number = |det K_B|
routes.text: All states have one permutation sign, so their number is |det K_B|, Tutte's magic number, the number of arborescences of each of the three trinity graphs.

routes.label: states form a distributive lattice
routes.text: Clock moves connect all states. The tree matchings are a subset of this lattice with no known description.

routes.label: uniform sampling of states
routes.text: Because all extensions of a partial matching have one sign, residual determinants count them, and a state can be sampled uniformly in polynomial time. This does not sample tree matchings.

routes.label: max-flow + planar density bound
routes.text: No separating triangle implies the Hall-type condition for two disjoint matchings, by bounding every component of T[U].

routes.label: Ore deficiency, minimal deficient set
routes.text: A minimal deficient set yields a non-trivial 3-edge cut. The balance |B'| = |F'| needed for Ore is not stated in the note.

routes.label: exact criterion: no black-inner separating triangle
routes.text: A pair exists if and only if t0 lies on the black side of every separating triangle.

routes.label: criterion checked on all roots to 16 vertices
routes.where: lim/code/campaign.py 14 (1206 roots); con/VERIFICATION.md (77 runs); gt (all 7868 rooted instances up to 16 vertices against max-flow)
routes.text: Pair existence agrees with absence of a black-inner separating triangle at every root tested.

routes.label: Li's Lemma 9 already gives the black inner boundary
routes.text: For a minimal deficient set all three cut edges have their black end inside, so Li's proof gives (iii) implies (ii) of T Theorem 1.2.

routes.label: induction over local expansions
routes.text: Grow rooted Eulerian triangulations by vertex splits and show a pair survives each split.
routes.vivid: Would replace the flow argument by a local rule.
routes.test: For each expansion look for a local map from pairs to pairs; check on all pairs for n <= 15.

routes.label: every avoiding cycle comes from a tree matching
routes.where: posed in dep/skeleton.md A2; refuted by comb/ROUTES.md 12 (E8) and lim/examples/prism_recovery.json
routes.text: If every Hamiltonian cycle avoiding e0* came from a tree matching, known Hamiltonicity results would give pairs with no flow argument.
routes.lesson: The recovery map is injective and not onto. A cycle avoiding e0* always defines a state, and that state is a tree matching or has no partner at all. Most avoiding cycles are of the second kind (ratio up to 26).
routes.cex: Hexagonal prism (dual with 8 vertices): 4 cycles avoid the edge, 2 tree matchings.

routes.label: matroid union
routes.text: Two disjoint matchings as a basis of a union of transversal matroids.
routes.vivid: Expected to reduce to the same deficiency count. Recorded so nobody spends an afternoon on it.
routes.test: Write the rank formula and compare with O (3.1).

routes.label: roots not on a common face
routes.text: For every simple 2-coloured triangulation some triple of roots of three colours, not necessarily the corners of a face, admits two disjoint states. The categorical agent tested the two-root version: the obstruction moves and the recovery lemma fails without a root face (A.x2).
routes.test: On the smallest black-inner example (9 vertices, lim/examples/t9_0.json, outer face 2) enumerate all root triples and count pairs.

routes.label: pair counts depend on the root
routes.text: In plantri graph 12_2 one black root has 9 states, 10 pairs, 8 tree matchings; every other black root has 9, 2, 2.

routes.label: Euler + side count + bijection, on triangles
routes.text: B + W = 2I + h - 2, 3(B - W) = 2l - h and B = I + l give 2l - h = -3. T adds that the length is odd.

routes.label: the same count on hexagons of the spoke graph
routes.text: t_in = |C|/4 - 3/2 for an alternating cycle of the spoke graph. Same identity with t_in = l (dep/correspondence.md 3.2).

routes.label: reading: W = B + 1, degree -1 of the colouring
routes.text: With the vertex 3-colouring c, delta(v, w) = c(w) - c(v) mod 3. The identity says the disk of a directed state cycle holds one more white face than black faces; the colouring map has degree -1 on it.

routes.label: checked on every enumerated cycle
routes.text: All disk equalities hold on every cycle enumerated, with all outgoing choices for n <= 6.

routes.label: drop bijectivity
routes.text: Let each black face choose a corner with no injectivity requirement.
routes.lesson: With defect d = B - I - l the identity becomes 2l - h = -3 - 3d. The state condition is exactly d = 0. Every interior vertex must be covered once.
routes.cex: 9 vertices: a directed 4-cycle with delta-sum 0; vertex 8 is used twice, d = -1.

routes.label: integer lift of Kasteleyn's sign lemma
routes.text: The faces of the spoke graph are hexagons, 6 = 2 mod 4, which is Kasteleyn's condition. The common sign of all states uses only the parity part of the disk identity.
routes.vivid: The disk identity may be a flatness condition for a Z/4 or complex signing of spokes.
routes.test: Derive t_out - t_in = 3 from a flatness condition for such a signing.

routes.label: discrete Morse theory
routes.text: Read the state as a pairing of black faces with vertices in the disk and compute the degree from the unpaired cells.
routes.vivid: B = I + l looks like a cancellation of cells.
routes.test: Write the pairing as a discrete vector field and check that one white face is always left over.

routes.label: peel the disk
routes.text: Remove a boundary vertex with its matched black face and show 2l - h does not change.
routes.vivid: An inductive proof with a picture per step.
routes.test: Implement the peeling on enumerated cycles.

routes.label: Grinberg count made rigid by a matching
routes.text: 3(B - W) = 2l - h is a Grinberg balance in the dual; the bijection adds B = I + l.
routes.vivid: Places the one new lemma next to the oldest tool of the subject.
routes.test: State Grinberg's formula for the dual disk and compare term by term.

routes.label: Gauss-Bonnet form for any cycle
routes.text: For a state s and a simple cycle C avoiding the roots, B - W = 2m - h + 2, with m the boundary vertices whose matched face lies inside. The topology agent reports the orientation-free form W = B + 1 as proved (B.6); the status of this exact formula is in topo/ROUTES.md.
routes.test: Outcome pending in topo/ROUTES.md.

routes.label: phase i^J
routes.text: J = (1/3) sum of delta(r(t), s(t)) is an integer; both reversals change J by 2.

routes.label: (-1)^cw from local turns
routes.text: cw' = #clockwise - #counterclockwise cycles. cw' = -J (dep/correspondence.md 3.1).

routes.label: epsilon = (-1)^((n+J)/2)
routes.text: A real sign; moves (a) and (b) flip it.

routes.label: the three signs agree up to a constant
routes.text: i^J = i^(-n) epsilon, and Z(x) = i^(-n) times the sum of T's polynomials over exchange components.

routes.label: J is an integer by the 3-colouring alone
routes.text: 3J = sum c(s(t)) - sum c(r(t)) = 0 mod 3 because r and s are bijections. J is clockwise minus counterclockwise cycles of D, the total colour winding.

routes.label: the sign is a Leibniz sign
routes.text: After a gauge by the 3-colouring the sign of a pair is the product of the local turns delta, the sign of a term in an incidence determinant. The real sign is prod_t delta(r(t), s(t)).

routes.label: sign as a product of two dimer weights
routes.text: Write the local phase as alpha(r(t)) beta(s(t)) and get Z as a product of two incidence determinants.
routes.lesson: At a face with three non-root corners the two cyclic triple products of the phase have ratio -1, and any separated weight gives ratio 1. Disjointness of r and s is what stops the sum from being one determinant.
routes.cex: One black triangle with three non-root corners.

routes.label: height-function form of J
routes.text: The Q_s-reversal can change the cycle structure of D completely and J still moves by exactly 2.
routes.vivid: Suggests J(r, s) = g(s) - g(r) plus a term local to Q_s, like a dimer height.
routes.test: Fit g on the enumerated pairs of the n = 15 and n = 23 examples.

routes.label: involution: reverse a cycle of Q_s
routes.where: O Lemma 5.2; L iota_1; T beta, Prop. 2.1
routes.text: Cycles of Q_s are directed by r. Reversing one chosen from s alone changes r, keeps the weight and flips the sign. T classifies all components: the number of partners is 0 or 2^k.

routes.label: twisted incidence determinant of Q_s
routes.text: For fixed s the partner sum is kappa det N_s, where N_s is the incidence matrix of Q_s reduced at the roots. It vanishes exactly when Q_s has a cycle. Lemma 5.2 is 'the rows of an incidence matrix around a cycle are dependent'.

routes.label: support of the multivariate polynomial
routes.text: With one variable per incidence, F(w) has coefficient +1 or -1 on each tree matching and 0 on every other state. So CT F(w)F(1/w) is the number of tree matchings.

routes.label: quartic Berezin integral
routes.text: F(w) is a two-species Grassmann integral with one quartic term per black face. It has an exact Gaussian decoupling, with no assured sign.

routes.label: checked on every cyclic second state
routes.text: Every state with a cycle in Q_s has zero signed partner sum; the partner count is 2^k or 0 on 140358 states (comb/lab/extra2.py 16).

routes.label: choose the cycle using r
routes.text: Let the reversed cycle depend on the partner.
routes.lesson: The reversal changes r, so a rule that reads r need not pick the same cycle on the way back. The choice must be a function of s. No smallest counterexample was searched.
routes.cex: none recorded; the argument is a proof that the involution property can fail, not an instance

routes.label: Taylor coefficient of order cmin
routes.text: Unit circulations from dual paths, a slide of edges onto spokes, Z(x) = sum over D of prod (-i e^{xL+} + i e^{xL-}); the coefficient of x^cmin is a nonzero multiple of a positive sum.

routes.label: second involution on marked objects
routes.text: Weights are signed crossings of vertical rays. A sign-reversing involution on lists of cmin marks; its fixed points share a sign. For cmin > 1 three verifications are left to the reader (dep/audit-li.md).

routes.label: integer polynomial per exchange component
routes.text: Integer weights 0 <= a <= 6n; Z_C(z) = sum eps z^omega has a nonzero coefficient of (z - 1)^m. Every exchange component contains tree pairs of both signs.

routes.label: marked walk (Garsia-Milne)
routes.text: Alternate the two involutions on tokens; the walk ends at a tree pair or restarts with fewer D-cycles. Never computes cmin. 2^O(n log n) time.

routes.label: heights as test functions, no weights
routes.where: comb/PROOF.md Sections 2-3 (Theorem B); refc/REWRITTEN-PROP-5-1.md (self-contained rewrite by the referee)
routes.text: Test the signed measure against a product of cmin heights at white faces. Pairs with one D form a cube, partners of one s form a cube, and the product is a cmin-fold difference that survives only on covers with exactly cmin cycles.

routes.label: linear weights 1 + x a
routes.where: dim/PROOF.md 7; refd/SIGNIFICANCE.md Section 2 (full proof with real signs and parity only)
routes.text: Replace e^{xa} by 1 + xa. The polynomial has degree at most n and the same leading coefficient; on the forest side it is a signed elementary symmetric moment. The Lean proof uses the same polynomial (lean/DIFFERENCES.md item 16).

routes.label: spoke weights are a height function
routes.text: omega(s) is the volume under the height of s, and L+(C) - L-(C) is the number of white faces inside C, which is B + 1.

routes.label: leading coefficient checked exactly
routes.where: con/supplemental.py (49 groups); comb/lab/dets.py 12; dim/code/linear.py; refd/code/results.json; lean/REPORT.md item 5 (71224 rooted triangulations up to 18 vertices)
routes.text: The first nonzero coefficient equals the signed sum of products of enclosed face counts on every instance tested.

routes.label: zero, vertex-only or face-only weights
routes.text: Use weights alpha_t + beta_v, or none.
routes.lesson: Such weights are pure gauge: every state has the same total, and the signed count is 0 = 0. What is needed is positive circulation on cycles, not positive weights.
routes.cex: Cube (octahedron dual, 6 vertices): two pairs with J = +1 and -1, Z = i - i = 0.

routes.label: parity or mod p count without weights
routes.where: comb/ROUTES.md 8; dep/skeleton.md D3; alg/PROOF.md 2; alg/TABLES.md (residues mod 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 11)
routes.text: Show the number of tree matchings is odd, or nonzero mod p.
routes.lesson: The number of tree matchings is always even (the two signs balance), and T = P - 2 N_1 mod 4 is compatible with T = 0. The weighted sum is the refinement that works; the first degree at which anything survives is cmin. No modulus among 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 11 gives a universally nonzero residue; the positive counts seen are 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 22.
routes.cex: Octahedron: 2 tree matchings, signed count 0.

routes.label: tree pair among the fewest-cycle pairs
routes.where: dep/skeleton.md D2; comb/ROUTES.md 7 (E2d, E3); refc/REFEREE.md; gt/ROUTES.md O3 (a 40-vertex one-cycle cover with no tree pair)
routes.text: Among the pairs with the fewest D-cycles one has Q_s a forest; or every cycle cover D has a forest orientation.
routes.lesson: Reversals inside one fixed cycle cover cannot be guaranteed to reach a forest pair, so a proof must move between covers. The leading coefficient is nonzero because of the fewest-cycle covers, but the surviving pairs can live in other covers. A statement that held on 1794 cases failed at the next size. (Scope as corrected by the referee.)
routes.cex: 16 vertices, class 158, t0 = (2,7,3): a single 13-cycle whose two orientations both have a triangle in Q_s; its 12 tree matchings lie in two other covers. Also the octahedron with every face split in four (n = 15).

routes.label: highest or lowest partnered state
routes.where: comb/ROUTES.md 4 (E1, E1c); refc/REFEREE.md; gt/ROUTES.md O1 (extremes of the whole matching lattice fail at 10 vertices)
routes.text: The top (bottom) partnered state of the lattice is a tree matching.
routes.lesson: For an extreme s every D has all cycles one way, but reversing a cycle of Q_s changes the number of D-cycles by two and extremality does not forbid it.
routes.cex: 12 vertices, class 6, t0 = (2,7,3) for the highest state, and its mirror image for the lowest (the referee's correction: the author's enumeration identified reflections and reported 14).

routes.label: minimal cover, all cycles one way
routes.text: Take D with cmin cycles and orient all of them counterclockwise (or clockwise).
routes.lesson: The leading coefficient sums over all minimal covers and prefers no orientation.
routes.cex: 12 vertices, class 6, t0 = (2,7,3) for counterclockwise, and its mirror image for clockwise (referee's correction; the author reported 13).

routes.label: largest rank difference
routes.text: The pair maximising omega(s) - omega(r) is a forest pair.
routes.lesson: Maximality forces the cycles of Q_s to be counterclockwise and nothing more.
routes.cex: 12 vertices, class 6, t0 = (2,7,3).

routes.label: one cycle always suffices
routes.text: cmin = 1, so a first-order argument is enough.
routes.lesson: cmin reaches 3 without separating triangles (192 of 3374 rooted cases up to 16 vertices) and 4 with them. A first-order argument is not enough and Li's Appendix B is needed. Unboundedness of cmin is not proved.
routes.cex: 9 vertices: octahedron with an octahedron glued into a face, cmin = 2.

routes.label: cubes of tree matchings; sign = parity of rank
routes.text: Tree matchings split into cubes of dimension cmin; or eps(s) = (-1)^omega(s) up to a constant.
routes.lesson: Z(q)/(q - 1)^cmin can have mixed signs, which refutes a rank-compatible signed cube decomposition. An abstract partition into cubes of dimension cmin is refuted by cardinality (referee).
routes.cex: Signs: 14 vertices, class 24, face 6, Z = -1 + 2q + q^5 - 2q^6. Cardinality: a 13-vertex instance with 6 tree matchings and cmin = 2 (refc/code/cube_cardinality.json). Sign = parity of rank fails at 8 vertices.

routes.label: ordinary determinant, all face variables 1
routes.text: Evaluate det(sum_t M_t) with no coefficient extraction.
routes.lesson: Without extraction a black face can supply two transitions and another none; the extra terms can cancel the answer. Testing only the cube or the octahedron would have hidden this.
routes.cex: Hexagonal prism dual (8 vertices): squarefree coefficient 45/64 at z = 5/4, all-one evaluation 0.

routes.label: allow doubled edges (standard double dimers)
routes.text: Add a diagonal so that r and s may share edges, as in Kenyon's double-dimer determinant.
routes.lesson: Nonvanishing becomes too easy: F_lambda(1) = lambda^n times the number of states, which is positive even with no pair. An SL2 connection does not kill doubled edges.
routes.cex: A rooted 9-vertex gluing with 4 states, no pair, doubled value 4.

routes.label: positive semidefinite blocks
routes.text: Find a gauge in which the local matrices M_t are positive semidefinite, then use mixed-discriminant positivity.
routes.lesson: Each block is, after multiplication by i, Hermitian of trace zero and rank two, signature (1, 1, 0). No similarity or congruence changes that. The determinant explains the cancellation and does not replace the planar positivity.
routes.cex: Any black face with two or three non-root corners.

routes.label: Combinatorial Nullstellensatz
routes.text: Get a nonzero evaluation of F from the coefficient form of Alon's theorem.
routes.lesson: Naming a nonzero monomial of F already names a tree matching. Substituting w = a_t b_v kills F.
routes.cex: Any instance: F(a_t b_v) = 0.

routes.label: real stability of the tree-state polynomial
routes.text: The unsigned generating polynomial of tree matchings is real stable, like spanning-tree polynomials.
routes.lesson: Projecting onto matchings destroys stability.
routes.cex: Cube: abc + def vanishes at a = b = c = e^{i pi/6}, d = e = f = i.

routes.label: mixed determinant with positive curvature
routes.text: Z = [prod z_t] det(sum z_t M_t) is n! times a mixed discriminant of rank-two blocks. Prove it nonzero from structural hypotheses.
routes.vivid: At a = 1 the matrix is the adjacency matrix of T[X] with a U(1) connection of holonomy i around black and -i around white triangles.
routes.test: Compute rank(sum over S of W_t) against |S| on cases with and without pairs; look for a non-diagonal normalisation.

routes.label: 2-adic evaluation at z = -1
routes.text: Choose weights with every L+ - L- odd and evaluate T's polynomial at -1.
routes.vivid: A count mod powers of 2 that sees the weights.
routes.test: Check on the examples whether such weights exist and the value is nonzero.

routes.label: cycle popping, random walk
routes.text: The two moves pop cycles of Q_s and of D, as in Wilson's algorithm. Show the walk hits a tree pair fast.
routes.vivid: All 320 random and greedy trials from ten bad starts ended within ten moves (con, COMPUTED, small sample).
routes.test: Measure hitting times on exchange components of growing size; look for a potential.

routes.label: Pfaffian gadget for the turn tensor
routes.text: Replace each black face by a planar matchgate with signature q^delta on distinct ordered corners and zero on equal corners.
routes.vivid: Would remove the coefficient extraction and give a polynomial-time evaluation.
routes.test: Check the Grassmann-Pluecker identities of the six-value signature with the boundary order fixed.

routes.label: height potential on pairs
routes.text: A combination of the two state heights that decreases along some exchange move at every non-tree pair.
routes.vivid: Would turn existence into descent.
routes.test: Search for a non-tree local minimum of each candidate on small exchange graphs.

routes.label: curved double-dimer connection, Lee-Yang
routes.text: Realise the loop factor -i e^{xL+} + i e^{xL-} as the trace of a non-flat connection.
routes.vivid: Each loop factor is -2i e^{xm} sinh(x Delta/2); zeros lie on the imaginary axis loop by loop.
routes.test: Solve the connection equations on two bipyramids and test trace identities on nested loops.

routes.label: LGV after cutting along seams
routes.text: Cut the pair diagram into non-intersecting paths and use a Lindstrom-Gessel-Viennot determinant.
routes.vivid: A fixed path matrix would make the sum a single determinant.
routes.test: Do the cut on the cube and on the first instance with two D-cycles.

routes.label: abstract valuation theorem
routes.text: Axiomatise: a finite signed cycle system, two involutions, a positive circulation.
routes.vivid: Would say which planar hypotheses do the work.
routes.test: List the axioms and find the first one that fails on a torus or a disk with four roots.

routes.label: a test function with one sign on all covers
routes.text: There is a test function of s for which every cycle cover contributes with the same sign, so that no minimum over the number of cycles is taken.
routes.test: On the 479 cases with more than 2^cmin tree matchings (comb/data/rows_v16.json), search low-degree polynomials in the heights.

routes.label: flux on a small set of faces
routes.text: Put positive flux only on a set of faces that meets the interior of every feasible D-cycle.
routes.vivid: Smaller weights, smaller degrees.
routes.test: Compute minimum hitting sets of cycle interiors on the enumerated instances.

routes.label: two evaluations of one sum
routes.where: O Prop. 5.1; L Key Lemma 7; T Thm 5.2
routes.text: Supported on forest pairs, and not zero.

routes.label: at least 2 cmin tree matchings
routes.text: The signed measure on tree matchings kills all polynomials of degree below cmin in the rank, and the two signs are equally frequent.

routes.label: at least 2^cmin tree matchings
routes.text: Every rooted triangulation with a pair has at least 2^cmin tree matchings. True for all 5088 cases up to 16 vertices; equality in 4609.
routes.test: Find a rooted triangulation with a pair and fewer than 2^cmin tree matchings; start at 17 vertices with cmin = 3.

routes.label: exactly one tree matching is impossible
routes.text: The signed unweighted sum over tree matchings is zero, so their number is even. The cube has two.

routes.label: tree matchings can be exponentially rare
routes.where: lim/HYPOTHESES.md (rarity); code/rarity.py q <= 6; cat/PROOF.md Prop. 6 (states, pairs and tree matchings multiply under insertion into a white face)
routes.text: Gluing q hexagonal-prism duals into white faces gives 3^q states and 2^q tree matchings.

routes.label: a canonical forest pair
routes.text: Under a bijection from states to trinity arborescences, tree matchings have a tree description that singles one out.
routes.test: Write the Hine-Kalman bijection on the 12-vertex class 6 example where every extremal rule fails, and look at the images of its 8 tree matchings.

routes.label: prescribed-degree spanning tree of H
routes.text: [y^{d*}] det L_H(y) is the number of tree matchings: a positive coefficient of the tree-degree polynomial. Existence would follow from a support theorem for that polynomial.

routes.label: label-transversal white trees
routes.text: Tree matchings are the spanning trees of the restricted white-face graph whose edge labels use every t and every v once. A doubly squarefree coefficient of a Laplacian determinant counts them, by Cauchy-Binet with all terms nonnegative.

routes.label: three-matroid intersection
routes.text: A tree matching is a common basis of the stated three matroids. The natural triple is irredundant. This does not rule out a different two-matroid encoding or a min-max theorem.

routes.label: unique partner: |det K_{B-s}| = 1
routes.text: Zeroing the entries of s in K_B gives a determinant equal to the number of partners up to sign. A tree matching is a state where it is 1.

routes.label: tree matchings = partnered Hamiltonian cycles
routes.where: comb/PROOF.md Prop. 7; lim/HYPOTHESES.md; gt/PROOFS.md Thm 7.2 (explicit left inverse; image = partitions with acyclic white parent map)
routes.text: Tree matchings are in bijection with the Hamiltonian cycles avoiding e0* whose state has a partner. So 3 #TM <= #HC(G).

routes.label: rooted functional orientations; two-sided hypertrees
routes.text: Two more exact restatements of the target, as an orientation problem and as a simultaneous hypertree realisation.

routes.label: matching matroid meets graphic matroid
routes.text: Treat the two endpoint constraints as one matroid and use Edmonds' two-matroid intersection.
routes.lesson: Matchings are not a matroid (augmentation fails on K_{2,2}). With only the face partition and the white graphic matroid, the augmenting-path algorithm returns white trees that repeat vertices.
routes.cex: Hexagonal prism: 4 of the 6 common bases of the two-matroid relaxation are not states (referee's correction, refd). Larger witness: truncated octahedron, eleven spokes repeating non-roots 3 and 4 (con/data/other_candidates.json).

routes.label: unconstrained white spanning trees
routes.text: Every spanning tree of the white-face graph, or of its restriction to duals of B, gives a tree matching.
routes.lesson: Both label constraints are needed. Rejection sampling accepted 0 of 100 trees on the larger named graphs.
routes.cex: Octahedron: 128 white trees, 8 after restricting to duals of B, 2 tree matchings.

routes.label: trinity arborescences = tree matchings
routes.text: The Hine-Kalman bijection carries all states to arborescences; perhaps every arborescence is a tree matching.
routes.lesson: Arborescences count all states. Tree matchings are a proper subset with no known one-colour criterion.
routes.cex: Hexagonal prism dual: 3 arborescences in each colour, 2 tree matchings.

routes.label: Yutsis partition of G
routes.text: Identify the two induced trees with a Yutsis decomposition of the cubic graph.
routes.lesson: Different ground sets: the vertices of G against the vertices of T.
routes.cex: definitional

routes.label: support of the tree-degree polynomial
routes.text: Show the target degree vector d* lies in the support of det L_H(y), from plane incidence inequalities.
routes.vivid: An unsigned target: no cancellation to explain. If every lattice point of the degree polytope were realised (P9), convexity would finish.
routes.test: Enumerate H-trees on the cube and the hexagonal bipyramid; compare the support with the lattice points of its convex hull.

routes.label: spanning-tree parity / matroid parity
routes.text: 'Each black centre keeps exactly two of its three spokes' looks like the spanning tree parity problem that Feder and Subi solve in polynomial time for 2- and 3-sided faces.
routes.vivid: If it is a matroid parity instance, Lovasz gives a polynomial algorithm, against 3^(N/4).
routes.test: Design the gadget for one black centre and two adjacent centres; enumerate feasible parity solutions against partial spoke choices.

routes.label: Bernardi process, Schnyder woods, blossom trees
routes.text: A canonical tree or orientation of the map might produce a tree matching directly.
routes.vivid: Each theory uses three colours and rooted trees on triangulations, as the target does.
routes.test: On the octahedron and the hexagonal bipyramid, test every facewise corner rule for bijectivity on X and for the forest condition.

routes.label: order-theoretic position in the state lattice
routes.text: Outcome (topo): the tree matchings are neither an interval nor an antichain of the clock lattice, and the top and bottom states are often tree matchings. No order-theoretic pattern was found.
routes.test: Decided on the topology agent's sample (166 lattices); a description of the subset is still missing.

routes.label: describe partnered Hamiltonian cycles in G alone
routes.text: There is a description, without states, of the Hamiltonian cycles of G avoiding e0* whose state has a partner.
routes.test: For the hexagonal prism list the 2 partnered and 2 unpartnered avoiding cycles and compare their face sequences; then test any candidate rule on the 176726 unpartnered cycles of the survey.

routes.label: out-degree count
routes.where: O Lemma 6.1; L Lemma 8; T (3), Prop. 2.1, Thm 1.2
routes.text: A tree component with v vertices and a roots has v - a out-edges and v - 1 edges, so a = 1. T: s is a tree matching iff it has exactly one partner.

routes.label: unique partner checked on 140358 states
routes.text: Brute force over all states: tree matching iff exactly one partner; the partner count is 2^k or 0.

routes.label: a forest state is enough
routes.text: Call s good as soon as Q_s is acyclic, with no partner assumed.
routes.lesson: Without the partner the out-degree count is unavailable: a component can hold two roots and another none. 'Forest', 'cycle-breaking' and 'tree matching' agree for pairs and differ for single states.
routes.cex: Hexagonal prism dual: all 3 states have acyclic Q_s, only 2 are tree matchings.

routes.label: tree-cotree duality
routes.text: The duals of the deleted spokes form a spanning tree on the white faces.

routes.label: Temperley / Kenyon-Propp-Wilson
routes.text: Read the step as the tree-to-matching bijection of KPW.
routes.vivid: KPW applied to the white graph encodes all its spanning trees and carries the label constraints along; it does not identify those dimers with B (dim).
routes.test: Write the bijection for the octahedron and the n = 15 example.

routes.label: orient towards y0
routes.text: Each tree edge is assigned to its end farther from y0 and selects the side of its black face bordering that end.

routes.label: the three papers select the same P
routes.text: Li's trace of the dual tree through black vertices gives the same set of edges of G.

routes.label: P is a forest, by the disk identity
routes.text: A cycle in P0 would be directed, and the selected-side count gives a disk with one black face fewer than the state requires. Then duality gives the cycle and the Jordan curve the two induced trees.

routes.label: innermost cycle, no disk identity
routes.text: If the complement had two cycles, an innermost one with no root face inside bounds a tree of faces, each with an out-step; some step is undone and two faces sit on one black vertex.

routes.label: W - B = 1 against W - B = 3
routes.text: The disk-identity argument restated as two incompatible counts of white minus black faces.

routes.label: forest certificate implies Hamiltonian cycle
routes.text: Conditional conversion: a spanning forest selecting one side per face has a complementary dual that is a Hamiltonian cycle.

routes.label: recovery is injective, with known image
routes.text: For fixed t0 and e0 the map from tree matchings to cycles is injective. Its image is the set of avoiding cycles whose state is a tree matching.

routes.label: recovery checked on every tree matching
routes.text: Every selected P is a two-component forest and both sides induce trees.

routes.label: remove a leaf of the white tree
routes.text: Removing a leaf of the white tree with the black face whose spoke it crosses leaves a rooted triangulation with a tree matching, and the cycle of the larger graph is a local detour.
routes.test: Implement leaf removal on the trees produced by dep/scripts/check_nodes.py and check validity of the smaller object.

routes.label: a potential along the selected out-edges
routes.text: Follow selected out-edges from a vertex to a root; a quantity that decreases along the walk proves connectivity.
routes.vivid: A third proof of the last step, perhaps the shortest.
routes.test: Compute the change of white-tree depth along each selected out-edge.

routes.label: Jordan curve theorem and Euler count
routes.where: O end of 6.2; T Lemma 7.1; APSW Lemma 5
routes.text: Each side of the cycle induces a connected acyclic subgraph of T.

routes.label: Li does not need the trees
routes.text: Li goes from P to the Hamiltonian cycle and glues cycles.

routes.label: induction with a prescribed cap edge
routes.text: Cut at a separating triangle, cap, solve one side, prescribe the same-label edge on the other, glue. O inducts on Theorem 2.2, L takes a minimum counterexample.

routes.label: cut only at black-inner triangles
routes.text: The exact criterion says when a cut is needed.

routes.label: Kelmans' reduction (1986)
routes.text: The reduction to cyclically 4-edge-connected graphs with an (x+ y+) or avoided-edge hypothesis was known. O re-proves it without citing it for this step.

routes.label: every separating triangle has one black side
routes.text: The state method needs no cut exactly when t0 is on the black side of every separating triangle. Changing the root or swapping colours can avoid cuts, not always.

routes.label: the gluing needs the same-label edge
routes.text: Trees of the two pieces meet in one vertex or one edge; prescribing the cap edge supplies the agreement. The smallest separating example has 9 vertices.

routes.label: prescribe whatever each cut needs
routes.where: Bagheri Gh. et al. 2022, proof of Thm 4.6; hist/WHAT-WAS-HARD.md 6
routes.text: Strengthen the induction hypothesis to an arbitrary set of prescribed edges.
routes.lesson: Hamiltonicity through an arbitrary prescribed edge set is NP-complete for Barnette graphs. The hypothesis must prescribe something bounded: one avoided edge.
routes.cex: reduction from Akiyama-Nishizeki-Saito instances

routes.label: a cut-free root
routes.text: Count how often some root (black face on the black side of all separating triangles, or the same with colours swapped) exists.
routes.test: Over generated Barnette graphs with several separating triangles, compute the fraction with a cut-free root; three triangles with alternating black sides should give the first failure.

routes.label: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 7.1
routes.where: O Thm 1.1, Cor. 7.1; L Thm 3; T Thm 1.1
routes.text: Every Barnette graph has a Hamiltonian cycle avoiding any prescribed edge.

routes.label: Lean formalisation (OpenAI repository)
routes.text: 31 Lean files, 8936 lines, importing only Mathlib. The formal statement is the conjecture as usually stated (lean/DIFFERENCES.md A). Corollary 7.2 and Theorem 2.2 are not formalised.

routes.label: consequences: P4 for Pfaffian braces
routes.text: The auditor could not open the cited theorem; the corollary is indeterminate in dep/audit-openai.md.

routes.label: all three proofs close
routes.text: Reverse-Lamport audits: O and T follow as written; L follows once four routine unwritten steps are supplied.

routes.label: ordered pairs of edges (global H+-)
routes.text: Some Hamiltonian cycle contains x and avoids y for any two edges. Not implied by the theorem.
routes.test: lim/data/strengthenings.json searched every edge pair on the small corpus; extend the search or find a counterexample across a 3-edge cut.

routes.label: an even number of avoiding cycles
routes.text: Every cubic bipartite graph has an even number of Hamiltonian cycles avoiding each edge.

routes.label: algebraic dual from grid minors (Lean)
routes.text: The formal proof never uses faces or the Jordan curve theorem. A drawn graph is a minor of a grid, the grid has an explicit algebraic dual, and duality survives deletion and contraction.

routes.label: Hall's theorem on a gadget; global density bound (Lean)
routes.text: Max-flow is replaced by Hall's theorem on a doubled incidence graph, and the density bound is proved for all of T[U] at once from a rank inequality.

routes.label: raw index sum, phase I^(n/3) (Lean)
routes.text: The formal proof never shows J is an integer. It keeps the sum of delta and needs only phase(n +- 6) = -phase(n).

routes.label: polynomial prod(1 + aX), weights from one flow on G (Lean)
routes.text: Z is a polynomial, not an exponential sum, and Lemma 5.3 is replaced by a single flow on G with charge +1 at every white vertex. Proved for an abstract triangle system with two hypotheses on cycle index sums.

routes.label: add a sink at the third root (Lean)
routes.text: Out-degree at most one and no directed cycle make a forest; no component count.

routes.label: the white tree is never built (Lean)
routes.text: The formal proof selects P inside G and skips the tree on the white faces.

routes.label: cut-balance lemma against the disk identity (Lean)
routes.text: A directed cycle of selected edges is a state cycle; a cut all of whose edges lie in a perfect matching contradicts |cut| = 2|black cut| + 3. No induced trees, no Jordan curve.

routes.label: glue perfect matchings across the 3-cut (Lean)
routes.text: Strong induction on the H- form: a perfect matching containing e with connected complement. Splitting is contraction.

routes.label: the Lean proof builds here; standard axioms only
routes.text: #print axioms gives propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. No sorry, admit, axiom or native_decide in the 31 files.

routes.label: one exact Euler identity, both directions
routes.text: m - b - (2p - 4) = (1/2) sum over non-face regions of (beta - (d - 4)). Every region contributes at most 0 except a black-inner separating triangle, which contributes +1.

routes.label: pairs are alpha-orientations (Felsner lattice)
routes.text: Pairs up to reversing D-cycles are the alpha-orientations of H - t0 with out-degrees 2, d_x - 2, d_r - 1. They form a distributive lattice.

routes.label: Hall-free shelling construction
routes.text: Build a pair by a canonical ordering from t0 inward, as for Schnyder woods.
routes.vivid: The certificate of non-existence is always one triangle, which is how density conditions behave when a shelling exists.
routes.test: Implement a shelling of the 55 triangulations up to 14 vertices and compare with the flow pairs.

routes.label: LP relaxation of the three constraints is integral
routes.text: Perfect matchings of B intersected with complements of spanning trees of H form an integral polytope.
routes.lesson: The natural LP is not integral. This does not exclude all encodings of the special spoke class; the broad hardness result is under polynomial Turing reductions.
routes.cex: A half-integral vertex at 13 vertices; minimality not proved. A feasible completion has one tree state and one non-tree state (structure referee INTEGRATION.md).

routes.label: induction by degree-4 expansion
routes.text: Lift a tree matching through the expansion of a degree-4 vertex.
routes.lesson: States lift bijectively, but the lift of a tree matching is a tree matching only under a side condition at the split vertex that is not inherited. Contraction can create the obstruction.
routes.cex: Contraction creates a black-inner triangle from 11 vertices on; not every tree matching lifts (708 of 1516 cases in gt/ROUTES.md I1).

routes.label: positivity of the norm or of the Laplacian terms
routes.text: CT F(w)F(1/w) and the constrained Laplacian coefficient are sums of nonnegative terms, so they are positive.
routes.lesson: Both are positive exactly when F is not zero, and showing that is the paper's argument. The positivity in the proof sits on the D side, these on the s side.
routes.cex: Obstructed roots of the double octahedron (9 vertices): 360 restricted white trees, 16 with one spoke per face, no tree matching.

routes.label: tree count as an unrooted invariant
routes.text: The number of tree matchings equals a fixed evaluation of a Tutte, Penrose, Tait or flow invariant of G.
routes.lesson: The count depends on the root.
routes.cex: plantri graph 12_2: 2 or 8 tree matchings depending on the black root, all roots with a pair.

routes.label: single-swap descent on the number of Q-cycles
routes.text: From every pair with a cycle in Q_s some single exchange lowers the number of cycles.
routes.lesson: A swap along a Hamiltonian D-cycle exchanges r and s, so it cannot lower the count both ways. Exhaustive data up to 15 vertices had made it look true.
routes.cex: 50 vertices, 4-connected (gt/code/data/deeptrap_50_1.json); two swaps suffice there.

routes.label: a global sign gauge on incidences
routes.text: Flip signs of incidence variables so that all tree matchings get the same coefficient sign.
routes.lesson: A GF(2) inconsistency certificate: six tree states in which every incidence appears an even number of times, three with negative sign.
routes.cex: A 13-vertex instance with six tree matchings.

routes.label: non-increasing exchange path to a tree pair
routes.text: From every pair there is a path of exchanges along which the number of Q-cycles never increases and reaches 0. A sign-free form of T Theorem 5.2.
routes.test: Search exchange graphs at 20 to 30 vertices for a pair with no non-increasing path; at 80 vertices look for pairs with no decrease within two swaps.

routes.label: Li's marked objects are the e_m coefficient
routes.text: Li's objects with cmin distinct marks are the elementary symmetric reading of the linear-weight coefficient.
routes.test: Enumerate Li's objects on an instance with cmin = 2 and compare the signed count with the coefficient of x^2 in F(1 + xa) for unit marks.

routes.label: parity is enough three times; the value 3 once
routes.text: In the real-sign form, reversing a Q_s-cycle or a D-cycle multiplies the sign by (-1)^length. So the cancellation, the forest lemma and the permutation sign need only that state cycles are odd. The value 3 is needed once, to align the signs of the minimal D groups.

routes.label: extremes of Felsner's lattice of pairs
routes.text: The claim that one of the two true lattice extremes always carries a forest pair is reported refuted. Independent replay is pending.
routes.test: Exhaustive census of Eulerian triangulations up to about 24 vertices, where one-cycle covers start to appear.
routes.lesson: Single-face terminal orientations need not be lattice extremes; even the true two extremes are reported insufficient. Test distance-one and irreducible replacements.
routes.cex: Reported at 18 vertices: 26 rooted instances in two triangulations. Provisional computation, no final report yet.

routes.label: finding a tree matching is in PPAD
routes.text: Each phase of the marked walk follows a path in a graph of degree at most 2 with alternating signs.
routes.vivid: Would place the search problem between polynomial time and the 3^(N/4) enumeration.
routes.test: Write one phase of T Theorem 5.3 as an END-OF-LINE instance with polynomial-size circuits for the two involutions.

routes.label: sharp primal hypothesis; gluing at black-inner cuts
routes.text: In G the obstruction is a non-trivial 3-edge cut whose black-ended side avoids b0. Li's cyclic 4-edge-connectivity is sufficient and not sharp: 1714 of 4494 rooted instances with separating triangles still have pairs.

routes.label: combinatorial Gauss-Bonnet with signed angles
routes.text: The state defines a flat signed-angle structure, and a vertex-local identity says turning equals minus colour winding. The disk identity is then the theorem of turning tangents. Orientation-free form: every chosen-edge disk has W = B + 1. Independently AI-refereed in the topology referee report; human checking pending. Apply the referee corrections where relevant. The proof uses Euler counting, not a smooth turning-tangents theorem. Boundary flatness and exclusion of the outer face are required.

review.verdict: Named claim checked with corrections in REFEREE.md; human check pending. Newly announced RAINBOW.md proof not inspected.

routes.label: cancellation as a Morse matching
routes.text: Pairs are combinatorial vector fields, tree pairs are gradient fields, and the cancellation reverses a closed orbit. The matching is acyclic and its critical cells are the forest pairs. Its Euler characteristic Z(1) is always 0, so a graded version is needed. Independently AI-refereed in the topology referee report; human checking pending. Apply the referee corrections where relevant. Correct grading: J = J_ccw - 2 times the number of clockwise Q-cycles. Pair each root with its outer-centre spoke in the Forman reading. Numerical checks of the Boolean levels only reach k <= 1.

review.verdict: Named claim checked with corrections in REFEREE.md; human check pending. Newly announced RAINBOW.md proof not inspected.

routes.label: Alexander duality: #cycles = 1 + b1(P)
routes.text: The complement of the 2-factor retracts onto P, so the number of cycles is one more than the first Betti number of P. Independently AI-refereed in the topology referee report; human checking pending. Apply the referee corrections where relevant.

review.verdict: Named claim checked with corrections in REFEREE.md; human check pending. Newly announced RAINBOW.md proof not inspected.

routes.label: sutured Floer support; point-rainbow white trees
routes.where: topo/REPORT.md item 3 (conditional on T Thm 1.2); COMPUTED on 826 instances up to 16 vertices; reft/REFEREE.md
routes.text: A tree matching exists iff a named spin-c structure is supported in the sutured Floer homology of the special alternating link of G (Juhasz-Kalman-Rasmussen), iff the white faces have a 'point-rainbow' spanning tree. Independently AI-refereed in the topology referee report; human checking pending. Apply the referee corrections where relevant. The referee announces a Rado/Euler proof of the point-rainbow criterion in RAINBOW.md, but that file was not yet present when integrated; that new proof was not inspected here.

review.verdict: Named claim checked with corrections in REFEREE.md; human check pending. Newly announced RAINBOW.md proof not inspected.

routes.label: local search from a point-rainbow tree
routes.where: topo/REPORT.md item 4 (R6'); 450 of 450 instances up to 16 vertices
routes.text: Same-colour exchanges from a point-rainbow tree, never increasing the black excess, reach a tree matching. A proof would be a cancellation-free local-search proof of the key lemma.
routes.test: Measure plateaus and step counts at 18 to 20 vertices (1543 triangulations at 18); look for a potential such as black excess plus a white-tree distance.

routes.label: the partner of a tree matching is a tree matching
routes.text: Swapping r and s would then be a free involution on tree matchings and explain why their number is even.
routes.lesson: The evenness is a signed cancellation, Z(1) = 0, and not a free involution. Forest pairs are not symmetric in r and s.
routes.cex: 6 failures among 442 tree matchings tested (topo data; smallest instance not recorded here).

routes.label: cycle-to-state map replayed; it is not injective
routes.where: map/spotcheck.py (bipyramids of rim 4, 6, 8, every edge of t0)
routes.text: Every Hamiltonian cycle avoiding e0* gives a state, and that state is a tree matching or has no partner. Two cycles can give the same unpartnered state: on the hexagonal prism 4 avoiding cycles give 3 states, on the rim-8 bipyramid 6 cycles give 4 states.

routes.label: boundary states of a cut; complete at lengths 3 and 4
routes.text: Cut T along a cycle, record a finite boundary state on each side, glue: the number of Hamiltonian cycles is the linear term of a Temperley-Lieb pairing of two disk vectors. O Theorem 2.2 says every piece with triangular boundary realises all 3 boundary patterns; for quadrilaterals all 6 patterns allowed by a parity rule occur (conditional on O; one sub-case by a finite computation).

routes.label: a uniform boundary condition for longer cuts
routes.text: Induct along cuts of length 5 or more with a boundary condition that every piece satisfies.
routes.lesson: The realised boundary patterns depend on the piece from length 5 on. The prescribed edge is the complete boundary datum of a triangular cut, and that is why the induction stops at separating triangles.
routes.cex: A piece with 9 vertices and a 5-cycle boundary (cat data); checked up to 13 vertices.

routes.label: two roots instead of a root face
routes.text: Root at two vertices not tied to a face; every root pair then has a two-root tree matching, and it gives a Hamiltonian cycle.
routes.lesson: Two roots move the obstruction and do not remove it, and O Lemma 6.2 needs all roots on one side of every selected cycle, which a root face guarantees. This is what the face root is for.
routes.cex: Existence: plantri graph 12_6, 51 of 66 root pairs. Recovery: a two-root tree matching with no Hamiltonian cycle at 8 vertices.

routes.label: the two cube structures form a bicomplex
routes.text: Treat reversal of Q-cycles and reversal of D-cycles as two commuting differentials and read the proof as homology.
routes.lesson: The two reversals do not commute. The homological packaging is a restatement and gives no new existence argument.
routes.cex: 12 of 624 pairs up to 12 vertices.

routes.label: topological Hall for partial tree matchings
routes.text: Get a tree matching from connectivity of the complex of partial tree matchings.
routes.lesson: The complex is not connected enough even in the smallest case.
routes.cex: Octahedron: a two-face subcomplex is disconnected.

routes.label: acyclic triangle factor of a second trinity K
routes.text: Hamiltonian cycles with a root on each side are the acyclic triangle factors of a second trinity K built from T. A symmetric restatement of the goal.

routes.label: every Hamiltonian cycle from a two-root tree matching
routes.text: With two roots allowed to vary, the state method sees every Hamiltonian cycle.
routes.test: Decide it at 13 to 16 vertices; if it holds, find the modified disk identity for cycles that separate the roots.

routes.label: contraction inequality tau(T) >= tau(T/ac)
routes.text: Contracting a degree-4 vertex never increases the number of tree matchings. An injection behind it would lift tree matchings along vertex splits.
routes.test: Look for a local rule extending a tree matching across a vertex split on the 948 cases (cat/code/recursion.py contract).

routes.label: primal proof with flows and real signs
routes.text: A full primal route using disk cut counts, linear-weight nonvanishing, recovery and 3-cut gluing. Author audit and finite checks exist; independent review pending.

routes.label: draft A: heights proof
routes.text: Manuscript route through signed intersection heights. The draft referee reports FOLLOWS with sentence repairs; this entry does not certify that every repair is applied.

routes.label: draft B: scalar height moments
routes.text: A manuscript route entirely in T. It uses the scalar height moment sum epsilon times omega(s)^m and an m-fold finite difference, then recovers via the tree of faces Y_s from Q_s plus two root sides. No plane spoke graph is needed. Author audit exists; final independent review pending.

routes.label: exact even-prism counts
routes.text: For a prism of order 4m: m states, two tree matchings, c_min=1 and normalized polynomial z^(m-1)-1. Full proof supplied, independent review pending.

routes.label: distance one from a lattice extreme
routes.text: Some element at rank distance at most one from a true extreme carries a forest pair.
routes.test: Enumerate true extremes and their rank-one neighbours through 24 vertices.

routes.label: join or meet irreducible pair cover
routes.text: Some join-irreducible or meet-irreducible lattice element carries a forest pair.
routes.test: Enumerate irreducibles and all cover orientations through 22 vertices.

routes.label: older approaches: tests in progress
routes.text: The final report gives a radial/permeating-tree dictionary and rejects a direct identification with H-s. A direct Pfaffian transfer still lacks balanced incidence objects, disk identity and recovery.
routes.vivid: A classical reduction could transport the missing root data.
routes.test: Replay the named prism, truncated-octahedron and Pfaffian tests when the report is available.

routes.label: Li two-mark involutions on running example
routes.text: 213 marked objects; iota1 fixes 141, iota2 fixes 9 of one sign; signed count -9. Closure, involutivity and sign reversal checked exhaustively on this instance.

routes.label: signed white area is additive
routes.text: The referee supplies a winding-number proof of height equals signed white area without separating triangles. This new proof has not itself had a second referee.

routes.label: unbounded c_min in Goodey chains
routes.text: End-rooted chains of k octahedra have k D-components in every pair, while primal faces have size four or six. Separating triangles are allowed. Author proof, not yet independently refereed.

routes.label: BF21 parity equals black-inner obstruction
routes.text: Identify the even-interior condition of the older contracted graph with the black-inner separator obstruction.
routes.lesson: The two conditions belong to different incidence constructions; the radial tree is not H-s.
routes.cex: Truncated-octahedron contraction, author certificate not yet independently replayed.
